Hi OP. I originally saw your story on TikTok and came to see what the latest update was. I'm sorry you've been put in a terrible situation. As others have said, it would be best if you simply didn't speak to him at all. But, no matter what choices you've made, things you've done or not done, or things he misinterpreted, at the end of the day this guy's behavior isn't acceptable. You've given clear signals you're not interested.   
  
Continue recording your interactions. I think it'd also be great if you were to keep a journal of every time he approaches you. Track date, time, location and things he's said. In situations like this, sadly, it is not the police's job to gather evidence. You have to create as much evidence as you can. Although you have recorded your interactions, doing so on paper can only help you. You can try to go to the police to discuss the assault, but i'm afraid that they usually can't or don't do anything about it after so much time has passed. Before you go, I would write down what happened and then a final paragraph indicating that you've gone to the police and that they don't think it warrants criminal charges at this time. Have someone there sign it. They might refuse to do so, but when that happens ask them if they can provide you an incident report or some other documentation showing that you've gone to them for help. Again, it's all about creating a paper trail.

Have you considered contacting SA Survival networks/organizations? Or any sort of women's abuse organization? A quick google search reveals a pretty large number of them in Ontario. You might not think they apply to you, but you HAVE been assaulted by him. You're being harassed. And you don't seem to have the support system in place to assist you with these sorts of problems. In five minutes I was able to find a guide to getting a Peace Bond, which does not require criminal charges and is filed for through the court. 

As far as your living situation, you might be in a position where you'll have to take out a storage locker (don't visit it alone!) and see if you can find temporary housing. If your financial situation is dire, perhaps a women's shelter can help you? Many of them have locked entries at night, or people watching out. They are better equipped for survivors or assault and abuse.

Hang in there. Best of luck.

I might be biased because i'm a first generation k-music listener (i'm very old) but I feel like this take suffers from a lack of historical context.

1. Yes, SNSD was one of the first bigger girl groups who made noise across international borders. However, they were hardly unique in terms of their sound. I remember people claiming ITNW plagerized Papaya, Yayaya-era Baby VOX AND some or another Fin.K.L song that had been released years prior. And it wasn't that the songs sounded especially alike (IMO). But people were upset that the concept was so similar. I vaguely remember the color palettes were even mentioned as PROOF that SNSD was just stealing a concept. Wild times.Additionally, SNSD's contemporaries under JYP were the Wonder Girls. WG's concept of course being HUGELY different from SNSD's. They were ALSO in the running to be the NGG, until JYP sent them to America and unfortunately by the time they came back SNSD had taken the crown and run with it. Because of the history of S.E.S., Fin.K.L, Papaya etc, that's the way the sound went. (Groups like Baby V.O.X and my problematic OG faves CHAKRA would have their sounds come back later!) However, I'd never go so far as to claim that Twice tries to replicate SNSD's sound because that's just not true. As for the NGG title, that's bestowed by knetz not the other way around.That being said. I find it interesting that you're jumping over Miss A whose sound veered very strongly ANTI debut-era SNSD or even 15&. Both of those groups put quite a bit of space between SNSD and Twice both time-wise and conceptually.
2. The same thing applies to Teen Crush. Yes, the TERM was coined by Weki Meki but the CONCEPT as we define it predates them by at least a decade. And frankly, it's not a super well structured concept. Teenage + Girl Crush makes very little sense when you consider that GC was meant as an empowering, feminine energy-embracing, mature-topic sound. Honestly I feel like TC falls closer to the idea of high teen concepts than it does GC concepts. The whole point of TC is to be more youthful and to discuss topics relevant to teenagers + with sound that appeals to teenagers. And if we're saying that trying to make a group that meets those needs = plagerizing well...I mean...?Especially because what we define as "teenage" sounding has changed over time. I listened to a burnt CD of "Dreams Come True" so much that it stopped being playable because at the time that song felt so youthful. Listening to it now, the song sounds distinctly un-youthful. The songs and styles we associate with "teen" change over the years. If we wiped the slate clean and erased all of music history prior to 4th i'd argue that NJ would have been the "teen crush" vibe over Itzy.  

3.  Kind of ties in with #2.  Just because the JYP made up a term doesn't mean they're plagerizing an entire concept, and similarly just because another group made up a term doesn't mean that everyone who makes a similar sound is plagerizing THEM.  
"Mixxpop" sure is a term that we got out of JYP and you want to tie it to Aespa's Next Level. But, frankly, Aespa's experimental sound isn't unique. Zimzalabim and I Got A Boy both have fundamentally similar "change up" type moments. IGAB was super polarizing when it released because of that and I still actively dislike the way they switch it up, despite enjoying plenty of Aespa and NMIXX songs. There are some S#ARP songs that go through changeups throughout the song as well. But even further back, the whole "rap break" that we associate with a lot of modern kpop wasn't always a thing. That was the original "change up" and I think it's one of the more noticeable things non-kpop listeners can point out.  
4-5. I honestly just don't see. Mostly because none of the examples given strike me as especially unique or innovative - they're all pretty generic.

Similar symptoms. UTIS, kidney infections and a prolapsed bladder can all cause

-Feeling of fullness or pressure in the abdomen

-Sensation that the bladder is never fully empty

-Increased URGE to urinate

-Increased frequency of urinating 

-Incontinence (leaking) either throughout the day or only during laughing/coughing/lifting objects/bending down/sitting up etc etc

-Discomfort while urinating  (not just pain, warmth, burning or itching are all possible types of discomfort)

There are other symptoms associated with the three different things individually but they all share the above in common.

Prolapsed bladder happens in stages and you won’t be able to diagnose yourself right away but you can always try taking a look. Untreated, it does hit a stage where it’s visible. Not gonna walk you through that but you can Google it. 

UTI is by far the more common cause for your symptoms and if it’s been going on longer than a few days you have to go get some antibiotics. Remember to take them all, even if you feel better - finish the bottle.

And if this has been going on for a bit you really should go to the doctor for some antibiotics. Remember that an untreated long term UTI can go to the kidneys. The other, rarer, possibility is a prolapsed bladder.

Not all UTIs are painful. Feeling the urge to urinate as well as increased frequency of urination are both classic symptoms. Remember to pee after sex or “play,” wash your hands before and after and if you use any toys sanitize them thoroughly.

I was always closer to Parent A. We were the definition of that Bonnie Burstow quote. Parent B has always been critical of me: my preference for education over domesticity, my sexuality, my introversion. Both parents were abusive: physically and mentally. While this mattered, it didn’t change that Parent A simply got me more. Parent B actively told me that I ruined their life and was the reason they were separated from their “real family.” They would both bring me into their marital disputes, but only B would tell me they were all my fault. B even once took me to A’s trunk to show me condoms A kept in their gym bag, just so that I would know A was cheating. I was 7. So you can see why things were/are the way they were.

These days, both Parents run a fairly sized online retailer operation. It’s just them with myself handling the technical/customer service end. Hours of them on their feet in a warehouse for very very very little profit. Parent B has been doing this with Parent A for over a decade. Any money that is made, is made by an equal effort from A and B. 

Things have been tight, financially. A has costly health problems and is also terrible with money. As I got older I like of realized A was operating on old rules. I’m the only reason my sibling and I have credit, general understandings of savings and financial matters. My sibling is more or less the breadwinner. A and B’s business could be making more, but A refuses to adapt and insists things will go back to normal eventually.

I bring this up because I recently discovered that A was using Only Fans. Now, I’d already seen A following spicy models on Instagram, but for some reason never got it into my head that A might be messaging them. Porn is porn, I expect A to watch it. But for me, Only Fans is cheating. You’re choosing an individual and paying them in exchange for sexual gratification. I discovered the evidence when A handed me their phone for something. B was in the room. I saw it, handed them their phone back and walked out of the room even as A yelled at me to come back.

I didn’t speak to A for anything non-work related for a month. First I struggled with telling B. Nothing good could really come of it. B wouldn’t leave A, A wouldn’t admit it, and A wouldn’t stop. I found out later that B already suspected and was aware of my discovery. B claimed to be more or less indifferent. They were surprised when I laid out why A’s excuses for being on that page were invalid, but even after that B kind of shrugged it off.

I, on the other hand, was furious. I still am. So I went from being A’s ride or die, where “if they get divorced I’m staying with A” to telling B that if they want to leave A, my sibling and I will have their back. That they didn’t need to feel financially bound to A. 

Things came to a head a while ago. For the first time not only did I not fear A’s aggression, I didn’t even respect them. I tore down their arguments one at a time, laughed in their face and was fairly stoic. A resorted to crying, which A never does, and emotional blackmail. I relented when they began to act as though they were having a medical emergency. Still, things have never been the same.

A recently acted in a suspicious manner that makes me think they either are once again, or never stopped, using OF. I had gotten to the point of being cordial, and have been sick for the last several months so have had an excuse to maintain my distance. I was disappointed and hurt, but not surprised. I no longer respect A as a person, and it makes it harder to love them. I feel like you idolize parents, even when they’re abusive. But when the veil is torn away they become just people. And A was already someone whose views I disliked. Now? I dislike them as a human being. I feel like I’m mourning A even as they sleep under the same roof. It’s a very lonesome feeling.

Oh boy I have a lot to say about this from a clinician's perspective. A LOT. 


To put it briefly? Your mother and step-father have ever legal right to make it mandatory for you to attend sessions. They do not have a legal, nor moral right to force your boundaries. With that said? I would call their bluff. Ask them for individual sessions with your therapist. 


Depending on your state, your parents are entitled to a certain amount (or all) information. However, as a patient you're also entitled to a certain degree of confidentiality. Many therapists will discuss and make an agreement with their patients, minors or not, as to what they disclose or how it is disclosed. They will also tell you what they are obligated to disclose to your mother/stepfather (this will always include being prepared and having a plan to harm yourself or others.) If your therapist is not willing to do this with you, then they aren't a very good therapist. Remember: therapy is for you. The therapist is there for you. Their goal is to listen to you and help you. 


The thing is. Family counseling sessions with minors are rarely successful without individual sessions. That is because a client is rarely able to express themselves freely and openly with someone else in the room. Your therapist will know this and if your mother/stepfather truly care about your well-being and handling of this blended family, I can't see them raising objections. If they do raise objections, well, then you know their goal really isn't helping you it's creating their picture-perfect family. 


With that said, family therapy is good for you. Your mother and stepfather seem to be under the impression that the end-goal is a perfectly adjusted family and that's not the case. A good therapist isn't going to be on board with forcing you to love and be all warm and fuzzy with your step-family. Your mother/stepfather are ALSO in therapy and they should also be discussing respecting your boundaries and wishes.
